A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeSplat and contain readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization and figure/table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original DeSplat reconstruction results, component and sensitivity ablations, qualitative examples, and computational measurements, including Tables 2–4 and A5–A6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds clean-scene reconstruction results, distractor-mask comparisons, and expanded computational measurements in Figure A12 and Tables A6–A9.

M1.justification: The static/per-view Gaussian decomposition, initialization, alpha compositing, densification, regularization, RGB representation, and optional appearance/background models remain unchanged. The added mask-threshold explanation documents visualization rather than changing training or inference.

E1.justification: V2 adds seven Mip-NeRF 360 scenes without occluders, covering indoor and outdoor environments while retaining RobustNeRF, On-the-go, and Photo Tourism. This substantially extends clean-input evaluation beyond v1's Yoda clutter-ratio experiment, without introducing a different reconstruction task.

E2.justification: The resource comparison expands from Splatfacto and SLS-mlp to also include Splatfacto-W, SLS-mlp with utilization-based pruning, and WildGaussians (Tables A7–A8). The FPS comparison removes SLS-mlp and retains Splatfacto (Table A9). Comparator membership in the retained accuracy tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify 2× indoor/4× outdoor downscaling for Mip-NeRF 360 and an opacity threshold above 0.5 for the mask comparison. Appendix B.3 changes the reported ablation GPU from RTX 2060 SUPER to Tesla V100; this does not establish that retained accuracy experiments were rerun. Existing training budgets and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure A12 adds direct distractor-mask comparisons on Patio High and Spot. The clean-scene evaluation tests whether decomposition unnecessarily damages reconstruction, while resource profiling expands from two scenes to the RobustNeRF and On-the-go suites. Existing component ablations, sensitivity studies, and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: There are no additions or revisions to reported run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The sensitivity plots retain their reporting format, and the added tables provide point estimates and across-scene averages without new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, 4, and A5 retain identical numerical entries. New Table A6 reports lower DeSplat PSNR than Splatfacto on all seven clean scenes, by 0.19–0.76 dB. Figure A12 adds mask findings, and Tables A7–A9 replace and substantially expand resource results. Revised timings do not establish same-setting changes relative to v1.

T1.justification: The rendering, compositing, loss, appearance-transformation, and background-model equations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical results or proofs; notation and explanatory wording changes do not alter the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: explicit static/distractor separation through photometric Gaussian splatting, fast rendering without pretrained semantic models, and compatibility with appearance and background modeling.

C2.justification: V2 attributes clean-scene degradation to fine textures, lighting variations, and reflections. It also qualifies rendering-speed comparisons across different frameworks and explicitly connects the persistent-distractor limitation to videos. The original Mountain/Patio failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the 0.5 threshold used for the existing Figure 8 masks, identifies Figure 7 as a Brandenburg Gate subset, and specifies Splatfacto-W-light with all functions enabled for resource comparisons. It also revises the reported GPU and documents the added dataset's preprocessing. Core implementation versions and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Mip-NeRF 360 and the gsplat library paper. The related-work categories, existing cited methods, and positioning of DeSplat's novelty otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes grammar, spelling, terminology, caption, and acknowledgment edits. The appendix separates experimental settings into B and results into C, moving future directions to D. Most exposition and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: The appendix gains the mask-comparison Figure A12 and Mip-NeRF 360 Table A6. The compact computational table is replaced by separate full-width memory, training-time, and FPS matrices. Existing Photo Tourism and failure figures are retained but relocated and renumbered, producing a substantial appendix display reorganization.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more informative clean-scene and mask validation, broader resource comparisons, and a useful qualification of cross-framework FPS comparisons. These strengthen the evidence while leaving the method and main accuracy results unchanged. The gain is limited by unreconciled memory-efficiency wording: Table A7 shows pruned SLS averaging 47.59 MB versus 72.49 MB for DeSplat's static model, contrary to the broad advantage asserted in the discussion.
